solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: It caters for visits re octane

definitions.text: It caters for visits re octane

indicators.note: To cater is an old word for setting something askew, diagonally, so the letters are moved about.

explanation.surface: A description of a place that looks after people calling in about fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay. "Caters" reads as providing for customers, but in its rare sense of setting askew it tells you to rearrange the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A service station is where motorists stop to fill up with fuel, octane being the measure of petrol quality.

clue.text: Not all there is can deter brat being troublesome

indicators.note: Something troublesome is unruly, so the letters are out of order.

explanation.surface: Someone half-listening wonders whether a bad-tempered child can be put off misbehaving.
explanation.walkthrough: "Not all there is" reads as one phrase; the definition stops at "there", and the anagram begins with "is".
explanation.definitionFit: Someone scatterbrained is disorganised and forgetful, not all there.

clue.text: Old instrument accountant used in novel

explanation.surface: An antique instrument has been hired by a finance professional for some purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: CA is a chartered accountant.
explanation.definitionFit: Rebecca is Daphne du Maurier's best-known novel.

clue.text: Law enforcers worried to act as go-between?

parts.note: as in something that ate at you, gnawed at you

explanation.surface: Police officers, anxious, are asked to mediate between two parties.
explanation.walkthrough: "Worried" looks like it should be an anagram of the police; it is ATE, as in worry eating at someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To interpolate is to insert something between other things, so it stands in the middle like a go-between.

clue.text: Small Frenchman gets up, leaving

indicators.note: In a down clue, getting up means reading from bottom to top.

explanation.surface: A short Frenchman rises from his seat and walks out.
explanation.walkthrough: Crossword Frenchmen are often a common French name, here Serge.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: egress is the formal, often legal, word for a way out or the act of going out.

clue.text: Pupil after school time in a work station

parts.note: a learner, as on an L-plate

explanation.surface: A student stays behind after lessons, working at a desk.
explanation.walkthrough: "After" places the pupil last even though it comes first in the clue; a learner driver displays an L-plate.
explanation.definitionFit: A terminal is a computer station where someone does their work.

clue.text: Queen's mate closed motorway

parts.note: as in a door pulled to
British motorways are numbered M1, M25 and so on; that the answer also reads backwards from the start of 'motorway' is a coincidence

explanation.surface: The consort of a queen is held up because the motorway is shut.
explanation.walkthrough: A queen is also a female cat; her mate is a tom. TO means closed, as when a door is pushed to.
explanation.definitionFit: A tom is a male cat, the natural partner of a queen, which is a female cat.

clue.text: Instrument in Volvo car I navigated

indicators.note: The answer sits inside the run of words that follows.

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a musical instrument lying in the Volvo they drove.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer spans four words, starting at the last letter of Volvo.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocarina is a small egg-shaped wind instrument.

clue.text: Gangster's weapon with last of ammunition in defeated warlord — about time

indicators.note: the letter from ammunition is placed in the word for defeated

parts.note: to see off or saw off a rival is to defeat them

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word ammunition is used
the warlord's title is placed about the abbreviation for time

parts.note: a shogun was a Japanese military ruler

explanation.surface: A gangster's gun, its last bullet loaded, is pictured beside a beaten warlord at a moment in history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Defeated' reads as describing the warlord, but it is its own piece: a phrasal verb for beating a rival.
explanation.definitionFit: A shotgun with shortened barrels is the stereotypical weapon of armed robbers and mobsters.

clue.text: Source of authority — a royal one with bite

explanation.surface: An authority figure is described as a monarch with teeth.
explanation.walkthrough: R is the common abbreviation for royal.
explanation.definitionFit: An arbiter has the final say, the one whose judgement settles things.

clue.text: Spirited item at tea dance needs bachelor

explanation.surface: A lively guest at a tea dance is in want of an unmarried partner.
explanation.walkthrough: "Spirited" suggests a lively person at the tea dance; it means soaked in spirit, and "tea dance" splits between the definition and the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A rum baba is a small sponge cake soaked in rum syrup, a spirited item to serve at tea.

clue.text: Investigator doesn't finish college

indicators.note: doesn't finish tells us the word stops short of its last letter

parts.note: a tech is a British technical college

explanation.surface: A detective drops out of college before finishing the course.
explanation.walkthrough: TECH is a British technical college; without its last letter it gives the slang word for a detective.
explanation.definitionFit: Tec is informal short slang for a detective, the person who investigates crimes.

clue.text: Cheers about one charged following provincial university's punishment

indicators.note: following means the pieces for cheers and the charged one come after the provincial word

parts.note: rustic means of the countryside, provincial

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word for cheers reads backwards

parts.note: ta is British informal for thank you, like cheers
an ion is an atom carrying an electric charge

explanation.surface: A cheer goes up as a provincial student is charged and punished by the university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one charged' looks like an accused person, but it is the physics particle.
explanation.definitionFit: Rustication is the Oxbridge penalty of sending a student away from the university for a time.

clue.text: Lousy batsmen I see being out a lot

indicators.note: Something lousy is poor and messed up, so the letters are jumbled.

explanation.surface: A cricket fan complains that the poor batsmen keep getting out.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket picture makes "out" mean dismissed; in the definition it means away from work.
explanation.definitionFit: Absenteeism is habitual absence from work or school, being out a lot.

clue.text: Argue about a boy

explanation.surface: Two people quarrel over a child.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the Latin-derived "regarding", as in business letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of making a case step by step, as in reasoning with someone.

clue.text: China to provide crew for old chopper

parts.note: china plate is rhyming slang for mate
to staff is to supply with workers

explanation.surface: The Chinese are asked to find a crew for an old helicopter.
explanation.walkthrough: "China" and "chopper" suggest a country and a helicopter. China is Cockney rhyming slang: china plate, mate. A chopper here is an axe.
explanation.definitionFit: A palstaff, or palstave, is a Bronze Age axe head, an ancient chopping tool.

clue.text: One may be Googling 'Brand, entertainer'

parts.note: to brand is to burn a mark, to sear

explanation.surface: Someone types the name of the comedian Russell Brand into a search engine.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital on Brand makes it look like the comedian Russell Brand; it is the verb, to mark by burning.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone Googling is searching the internet, a searcher.

clue.text: Sybil about to sing chorus knocking back traditional drinks

indicators.note: knocking back means the whole assembled word is reversed, read from the back
about means the seer's letters go round the singing

parts.note: a sibyl is a prophetess, a seer; the setter spells it like the name
to la-la is to sing a wordless chorus

explanation.surface: Sybil is about to join in a singing chorus while knocking back traditional drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocking back' looks like downing drinks, but it reverses SELALAER, the seer around LALA, to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Real ale is British cask-conditioned beer brewed in the traditional way, as championed by CAMRA.

clue.text: Redcoat's dashing style

explanation.surface: A British soldier in his red uniform cuts a stylish figure.
explanation.walkthrough: "'s" stands for is, joining wordplay to definition. A redcoat was a British soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the geometric decorative look of the 1920s and 30s is one particular style of design.

clue.text: Birds heading off for Scottish islands

indicators.note: The word loses its first letter, its head.

explanation.surface: A flock of birds sets off towards islands off Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: "Inch" is a Scottish word for a small island, as in Inchcolm.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland an inch is a small island, so inches are Scottish islands.

clue.text: Outside Scottish town is rustic farmyard feature

indicators.note: The word for rustic goes around the town.

parts.note: a country bumpkin; it goes around the town
the town on the Ayrshire coast

explanation.surface: A rural feature stands on the outskirts of a Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: Ayr is a town in south-west Scotland. The clue's order puts "Outside" first, but it acts on the town and the rustic.
explanation.definitionFit: A hayrick is a stack of hay, a familiar sight in a farmyard.

clue.text: Mischievous fellow and posh one make light conversation

explanation.surface: A prankster and an upper-class type chat together.
explanation.walkthrough: A nob is British slang for a posh person; a hob is a household sprite, as in hobgoblin.
explanation.definitionFit: To hobnob is to mix and chat socially, especially with the well-connected.

clue.text: Fashionable hero vetoing changes

explanation.surface: A stylish champion blocks proposed reforms.
explanation.walkthrough: "Changes" looks like the noun being vetoed; it is the verb that rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: this dated jazz-age slang for being with it, up to date, means fashionable.

clue.text: Sounds like greeting current in Somerset

indicators.note: Say the greeting aloud to hear the answer.

explanation.surface: A hello that is currently popular in the West Country.
explanation.walkthrough: "Current" means a flow of water here: the Yeo is a river in Somerset, a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: The River Yeo flows through Somerset, so it is a current there.

clue.text: Fiddlesticks made of Oriental woods

explanation.surface: Violin bows crafted from Eastern timbers.
explanation.walkthrough: Fiddlesticks look like violin bows made of wood; the word is an exclamation meaning nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are dismissive exclamations meaning rubbish, words you say when you don't believe a claim.

clue.text: Lapwing's regularly taken bit of cereal

indicators.note: Letters taken at regular intervals means picking them at evenly spaced steps, here every second one.

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of lapwing

explanation.surface: A lapwing, a bird, regularly pecks at grain.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the even letters of LAPWING are taken; the 's is part of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An awn is the bristle on an ear of barley or other cereal.

clue.text: Fixing pole, not very well

explanation.surface: Someone repairing a post makes a poor job of it.
explanation.walkthrough: "Not very well" reads as a comment on the fixing; it is AILING.
explanation.definitionFit: Nailing something is fixing it in place with nails.

clue.text: Boorish type in noble line to do damage to family

explanation.surface: An oafish member of an aristocratic lineage ruins his relatives.
explanation.walkthrough: RY stands for railway, a railway line.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the phrase names an awkward, unsophisticated rustic, the very picture of a boor.
